title: A reliable way to break malaria transmission through its vectors

concept.text: Concept synthesis: The innovation would be a durable, deployable way to interrupt malaria transmission by acting on the mosquitoes that carry the parasite. It could work by making major malaria vectors unable to sustain transmission, by safely suppressing their populations, or through another effective vector-directed approach. The defining achievement would be reliable interruption of transmission under real conditions; gene drive is one possible means of achieving that capability, not a requirement.

Scope synthesis: Reliability would require effectiveness across relevant mosquito and parasite populations, seasons and ecological settings. A successful intervention would need to account for resistance, movement of mosquitoes and infections between locations, ecological effects and community governance. These are proposed dimensions of the breakthrough, rather than capabilities established by the supplied evidence.

significance.text: Conditional significance: A durable intervention in vector populations could provide protection across a community and reduce dependence on preventing every infectious bite or protecting each person at every exposure. If it remained effective and could be deployed over the necessary area, its effects could persist between individual encounters with health services or protective measures. That population-level durability is what would make the capability revolutionary.

Conditional downstream possibility: Combined with effective treatment, surveillance and adequate coverage, reliable vector control could help enable malaria elimination in settings where existing interventions struggle. Elimination would still depend on identifying and treating infections and managing their reintroduction. Local reductions in mosquito transmission would not, by themselves, establish that elimination had occurred or would persist.

Impact limits, synthesized from the proposed concept: Population-level protection should not be read as automatic, universal or permanent protection. An intervention could affect only some vector species, lose effectiveness through resistance, or leave transmission pathways outside its geographic reach. Technical effectiveness would also need to be accompanied by acceptable ecological consequences, practical deployment and legitimate governance. The supplied evidence does not establish the achievable magnitude of these benefits.

missing_breakthrough.text: Proposed capability gap: The missing advance is dependable translation from a vector-directed mechanism into sustained reductions in malaria transmission and human disease across relevant endemic settings. Spreading an engineered trait, reducing a parasite measurement or suppressing mosquitoes would each be an intermediate achievement. None alone would demonstrate the complete public-health capability.

Scientific and engineering barrier synthesis: A population-modification approach would need both an effective transmission-blocking trait and a way to maintain sufficient coverage of the relevant mosquito populations. A suppression approach would need to keep vector abundance low enough despite reproduction and movement from surrounding areas. Either route would have to withstand biological variation, seasonal changes and resistance without creating unacceptable ecological effects. For a gene-drive implementation, the spread of the engineered trait and the persistence of its transmission-blocking effect would be separate properties to establish.

Deployment and governance barrier synthesis: The intervention would need a workable geographic deployment strategy, monitoring that can detect declining effectiveness or unexpected spread, and arrangements for responding to adverse findings. Movement across community or jurisdictional boundaries complicates both evaluation and authorization. These requirements belong to the proposed practical capability; the supplied source does not document their resolution.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes a relevant study to Carballar-Lejarazú and colleagues: “Dual effector population modification gene-drive strains of the African malaria mosquitoes, Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii,” listed as published in PNAS on 10 July 2023, with DOI 10.1073/pnas.2221118120. It describes engineered strains spreading in small cages and reducing parasite measures, with human-impact estimates derived from modeling. These are the research record’s attributions; the supplied review could not independently verify the article’s identity or scientific contents from the retained copy.

The earlier description of access as an abstract must be corrected. According to the supplied review, the retained material contains only a cookie interstitial and no article content. Although the source index records a saved artifact and marks it verified, that metadata does not establish that the abstract or scientific findings were captured. Consequently, the cage experiments, parasite results and modeling claims remain unverified within this evidence package. This access failure is not evidence that the reported results are false.

Interpretive synthesis: Even if the attributed study description is accurate, small-cage spread and reduced parasite measures would establish a narrower result than sustained reductions in malaria disease in open populations. Modeled human benefits would remain projections rather than observed field outcomes. The supplied material establishes no independently verified field demonstration of the full innovation and provides no usable account of subsequent progress through the review’s stated freshness target of 1 November 2026. It therefore cannot establish the present global state of the field.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration framework: Following staged safety assessment and authorization by affected communities and authorities, independently evaluated field studies should show sustained, substantial reductions in malaria transmission and human disease across multiple endemic settings. Before evaluation, investigators would need to define the intended magnitude of benefit, the duration of follow-up and the range of settings represented. The terms “large,” “sustained” and “several” are not operational thresholds, and these proposed criteria are not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained transmission and disease reductions across multiple endemic settings

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evidentiary requirements: Studies should distinguish changes in vector populations or traits, parasite transmission and human disease, and use appropriate comparisons to assess the intervention’s contribution alongside other malaria-control measures. Independent replication and transparent methods should make it possible to assess whether benefits recur across relevant mosquito and parasite populations and different seasonal and ecological conditions. Models could help interpret and extrapolate results, but projected benefits should remain separate from observed outcomes.
completion_criteria.label: Independently replicated benefits across relevant populations and ecological conditions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and practical boundaries: Follow-up should characterize resistance, loss of effectiveness, movement or spread of the intervention, ecological effects and transmission returning through migration or imported infections. A convincing demonstration should also state the deployment coverage, operational demands, geographic boundaries and governance arrangements under which the results were achieved. Finite studies could establish demonstrated breadth and durability over specified conditions and periods; they could not prove literal universality or permanent effectiveness.
completion_criteria.label: Follow-up characterizes durability and states practical deployment boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: INF-13, “A highly protective, durable and readily deliverable malaria vaccine,” is the closest complementary concept. Its supplied title identifies a vaccine approach to malaria prevention, whereas INF-04 acts through mosquito vectors. Both could contribute to reducing malaria burden, but success in one would not establish success in the other. The roster supports this high-level distinction; it supplies no detailed vaccine design, performance evidence or implementation criteria.

Roster-based comparison: INF-03, “A tuberculosis vaccine that interrupts transmission,” shares the ambition of reducing onward transmission and protecting populations beyond individual recipients. It concerns a different pathogen and an intervention delivered through vaccination. INF-04 instead requires an effective intervention in mosquito populations and evaluation of vector ecology and movement. The shared transmission goal does not make their mechanisms or completion criteria interchangeable.

Roster-based comparison: INF-05, “Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections,” could conceptually complement malaria control through better identification and management of infections, but it is a diagnostic capability rather than a vector intervention. INF-01, INF-08 and INF-09 concern vaccine protection or vaccine response capabilities for other infectious threats. Their broad prevention goals overlap with INF-04, while their target diseases, delivery mechanisms and engineering problems remain distinct. These comparisons preserve the separate roster entries and make no claims about their achieved performance.

unresolved_issues: The supplied retained artifact cannot verify the cited study’s identity, publication details, experimental methods, results or human-impact modeling.
The package provides no verifiable quantitative effect sizes, cage conditions, parasite endpoints, resistance findings or field outcomes for the attributed study.
No usable freshness evidence establishes subsequent developments through 1 November 2026; the innovation’s present global state cannot be inferred from this package.
The intended magnitude and duration of benefit, number and diversity of evaluation settings, and acceptable ecological and operational boundaries remain to be defined.
The supplied source does not document the underlying goal or establish consensus requirements; the explanatory scope and demonstration framework remain proposed synthesis.
The review’s blanket uncertainty about INF-13’s contents was narrowed using its explicit roster title. Detailed claims about that vaccine concept remain unavailable.

brief.title: Lasting protection from malaria by targeting mosquitoes
possible: People in places with malaria could gain lasting community protection by changing the mosquitoes that spread it. This could mean making mosquitoes unable to pass on the parasite, safely reducing their numbers, or using another approach that reliably breaks transmission.
why: Protection across mosquito populations could reduce dependence on preventing every infectious bite. Its effects could persist between visits to health services or uses of individual protective measures.
Combined with treatment and monitoring, reliable mosquito control could help communities eliminate malaria where existing measures struggle.

sources.showed: A gene drive, a system that spreads an inherited trait, spread through mosquitoes in small cages. The engineered mosquitoes carried genes that reduced parasite infections. Estimated benefits for people came from models.
sources.quote: The effector molecules reduced significantly both parasite prevalence and infection intensities.
sources.cited_for: This supports changing mosquitoes so that fewer carry parasites and infected mosquitoes carry fewer parasites.
sources.not_established: Small-cage results do not establish lasting reductions in malaria transmission or disease outdoors.

sources.showed: In a randomized trial in Malawi, house improvements and mosquito breeding-site management added no detectable benefit beyond standard measures. Researchers measured infectious mosquito bites, called EIR, and infections.
sources.quote:
Over the full trial period, the EIR did not differ 
between the four trial arms
sources.cited_for: This shows why added mosquito-control measures need comparisons that separate their contribution from existing protection.
sources.not_established: Very low transmission limited the trial’s ability to detect differences between groups.

sources.showed: A gene drive that blocks female reproduction caused mosquito populations to collapse in large indoor cages. The researchers found no resistance that restored the targeted gene’s function.
sources.quote: The gene-drive element spreads rapidly through the populations, fully supresses the population within one year and without selecting for resistance to the gene drive.
sources.cited_for: This supports mosquito suppression under more complex conditions than small laboratory cages.
sources.not_established: Indoor population collapse does not establish durable suppression outdoors or reduced malaria disease in people.

shown: Carballar-Lejarazú and colleagues spread parasite-blocking genes through mosquitoes in small cages. Hammond and colleagues collapsed mosquito populations in large indoor cages. These studies demonstrate biological mechanisms; benefits for human malaria remain unproven by these experiments.
missing: Field studies have yet to demonstrate sustained reductions in transmission and human disease across varied settings where malaria persists.
Protection must remain effective despite resistance, seasonal changes and mosquitoes or infections arriving from elsewhere.
Deployment must combine sufficient coverage, monitoring and community authorization with acceptable ecological effects.

milestones.label: Lasting reductions in malaria transmission and disease across settings
milestones.explanation: Following safety assessment and community and authority authorization, independently evaluated field studies would have to show lasting, substantial reductions across settings. This would establish protection for people.

milestones.label: Independent studies reproduce benefits across populations and environments
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would have to reproduce benefits across mosquito and parasite populations, seasons and environments while accounting for other control measures. This would establish how broadly protection works.

milestones.label: Follow-up establishes durability and practical deployment boundaries
milestones.explanation: Follow-up would have to track resistance, waning effects, spread, ecological effects and returning transmission, and state deployment and governance conditions. This would define where and how long protection holds.

uncertain: The required size and duration of benefit, and the range of settings needed to demonstrate reliability, remain undefined.
It remains unclear how resistance and movement between locations would affect lasting protection.
Acceptable ecological effects and practical deployment boundaries remain to be defined.

page.title: Interruption of residual malaria transmission by vector control
page.definition: An additional measure directed at malaria-transmitting mosquitoes helps stop transmission in a focus, a bounded area where local conditions allow the parasite to spread. Transmission had persisted there despite effective use of insecticide-treated nets or insecticide sprayed on indoor surfaces. Indoor spatial repellents have reduced new infections in children using treated nets. Interruption goes further: local mosquitoes cease passing the parasite to people, although infections acquired elsewhere can still be detected.

goal.need: In 30 communities in southwestern Mali, 93.2% of people surveyed used a net and 34% had malaria infection. Net users still received an estimated 11.2 malaria-vector bites per person per night, 7.1 of them outdoors. Nets protect people in bed, and indoor spraying reaches mosquitoes that rest on treated surfaces. Preventing infections in people exposed elsewhere depends on reaching the mosquitoes responsible for those bites. If local transmission stops, surveillance and measures to prevent its return are still needed.

statements.quote: to reduce the population of those species enough to stop the transmission of the disease.
statements.context: The species are Anopheles coluzzii, An. gambiae, An. arabiensis and An. funestus; the disease is malaria.

statements.quote: specifically designed to interrupt residual transmission and thereby address the practical limitations of existing interventions
statements.context: In Control of residual malaria parasite transmission, WHO called on industry to develop tools that target the mosquito populations sustaining transmission.

completion.title: An added vector intervention helps stop locally acquired malaria in a focus for more than three years.
completion.criterion: In a defined focus with transmission persisting despite effective use of treated nets or indoor residual spraying, comparative field evidence establishes that an additional mosquito-directed intervention contributed to interruption. Case investigation and surveillance document more than three years without a new locally acquired mosquito-borne infection, including one directly linked to an imported case. Investigators distinguish imported, relapsing, recrudescent and induced cases. Surveillance and measures against re-establishment continue.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis. WHO’s 2017 framework supplies the cleared-focus endpoint. No outside body was found to combine it with attribution to an added vector intervention.
completion.threshold_quote: There has been no locally acquired case for more than 3 years
completion.basis: Table 3 of WHO’s 2017 framework uses locally acquired cases. Table 4 of WHO’s 2025 surveillance manual uses indigenous cases for its operational time criterion and allows only imported, relapsing, recrudescent or induced cases in the current calendar year. The Atlas retains the 2017 rule: a new local mosquito-borne infection directly linked to an imported case also restarts the interval. Comparative evidence establishes the intervention’s contribution in the evaluated setting.

milestones.title: A vector intervention demonstrates transmission-reducing activity in controlled laboratory tests.
milestones.criterion: A controlled laboratory comparison shows a reduction in mosquito abundance, the mosquitoes’ ability to transmit the parasite, or mosquito contact with people, according to the intervention’s intended effect. For a spatial emanator, a relevant measure is the reduction in mosquito landings on people relative to a control.
milestones.set_by: WHO/TDR, Guidance framework for testing genetically modified mosquitoes, section 2.6.1, for suppression and modification. WHO’s Guardian efficacy assessment documents the laboratory comparison for a spatial emanator.
milestones.threshold_quote: the primary objective should be the potential for reducing transmission intensity

milestones.title: An added vector intervention significantly reduces human malaria infection in a controlled field trial.
milestones.criterion: A controlled field trial shows a statistically significant reduction in its prespecified human malaria infection endpoint relative to a control arm receiving the local standard of care. The trial specifies its target effect size and significance level in advance. Mosquito abundance, landings and infectious bites alone do not measure infection in people.
milestones.set_by: WHO, Norms, standards and processes underpinning WHO vector control policy development, sections on trial endpoints and epidemiological outcomes.
milestones.threshold_quote: a statistically significant epidemiological impact over the control arm

milestones.title: WHO recommends a vector-control class and prequalifies a product after epidemiological evaluation.
milestones.criterion: WHO assesses public health value, with at least two epidemiological trials required to initiate policy review; inconsistent findings can require more trials. WHO issues a recommendation, and product assessment establishes safety, quality and entomological efficacy for prequalification. On 13 August 2025, WHO conditionally recommended indoor spatial emanators alongside insecticide-treated nets, based on five studies, and announced prequalification of Mosquito Shield and Guardian. This establishes deployment eligibility for human–vector contact reduction.
milestones.set_by: WHO Global Malaria Programme and vector-control evaluation programme, Norms, standards and processes underpinning WHO vector control policy development, pages 8–10.
milestones.threshold_quote: a minimum of two trials with epidemiological endpoints is required to initiate convening the GDG.

milestones.title: A malaria focus has no indigenous case this calendar year and had its last one in the previous three.
milestones.criterion: Case investigation in the intervention focus documents no indigenous malaria case in the current calendar year and at least one in the preceding three calendar years. An indigenous case is locally acquired and has no direct epidemiological link to an imported case. This case history establishes the focus classification. Attribution to the intervention requires separate evidence.
milestones.set_by: World Health Organization, Malaria surveillance, monitoring and evaluation: a reference manual, second edition, Table 4.
milestones.threshold_quote: The last indigenous case(s) was detected in the previous calendar year or up to 3 years earlier.

milestones.title: A spatial emanator demonstrates end-of-life efficacy in three semi-field studies.
milestones.criterion: Three adequately powered studies in diverse geographic regions test wild, free-flying mosquitoes under simulated use conditions. At the end of the product’s intended life, the prespecified measure of protection must be statistically superior to the negative control. It must also show non-inferiority to an aged positive control or meet the prespecified epidemiologically relevant threshold. WHO gives a 30% reduction in blood feeding as an example for the threshold comparison.
milestones.set_by: WHO Prequalification of Vector Control Products, Module 5 implementation guidance for spatial emanators, sections 2 and 10.
milestones.threshold_quote: Three semi-field studies are required for Module 5 submissions, which must be conducted in diverse geographic regions.

milestones.title: WHO recommends an intervention class for malaria vector control after epidemiological review.
milestones.criterion: For a new intervention class, at least two trials with epidemiological endpoints are required to initiate convening the WHO guideline development group. Inconsistent or methodologically limited trials can require further studies. The milestone is reached when WHO publishes a recommendation supporting use of the class in a specified malaria setting.
milestones.set_by: WHO Global Malaria Programme, Norms, standards and processes underpinning WHO vector control policy development.
milestones.threshold_quote: a minimum of two trials with epidemiological endpoints is required to initiate convening the GDG.

milestones.title: WHO lists an individual malaria vector-control product as prequalified.
milestones.criterion: An applicable WHO recommendation covers the product class. WHO assesses the individual product’s safety, quality and efficacy and includes the product in its list of prequalified vector-control products.
milestones.set_by: WHO Prequalification Unit, Overview of the WHO Prequalification Assessment of Vector Control Products.
milestones.threshold_quote: included in the WHO list of prequalified VCPs.

not_found: No outside-body test combining residual-focus clearance with attribution to an individual vector intervention was found.
No universal entomological effect-size or trial significance threshold covering every vector-control approach was found.
No cited intervention study established the completion test.
No malaria programme or advisory committee statement was found disputing the value or feasibility of interrupting residual transmission in a defined focus.

results.finding: Across four laboratory replicates, AgTP13 mosquitoes showed an approximately 54% reduction in parasite prevalence.
results.detail: Homozygous mosquitoes were compared with control lines in parasite challenge assays. The study also found reduced infection intensity.
results.quote: Both AgTP13 hemi- and homozygous adult females exhibited strong parasite suppression with oocyst prevalence reduced from ~74% in controls to 44.2% (hemizygotes, ~40% reduction) and 33.9% (homozygotes, ~54% reduction)

results.finding: WHO prequalified two spatial emanators, Mosquito Shield and Guardian, alongside a recommendation for malaria vector control.
results.detail: The announcement reports the recommendation and prequalification, including quality, safety and efficacy assessments. It does not describe the epidemiological trials or the conditions of the recommendation.
results.quote: WHO has prequalified the first two spatial emanators products, Mosquito Shield and Guardian, manufactured by SC Johnson & Son, Inc., alongside the publication of the WHO recommendation supporting the deployment of this intervention class in vector control programmes for malaria.

results.finding: WHO conditionally recommends larviciding as a supplementary malaria-control intervention; number of epidemiological trials not stated.
results.detail: Larviciding reduces vector density, but the excerpt does not report epidemiological trials supporting the recommendation or prequalification of a larviciding product.

Insecticides can be regularly applied to water bodies (larviciding) for the prevention and control of malaria in children
and adults as a supplementary intervention to ITNs or IRS in areas with ongoing malaria transmission where aquatic
habitats are few, fixed and findable.

results.finding: In a six-cage Anopheles gambiae study, all four gene-drive cages reached complete population suppression within 245–311 days.
results.detail: The study used cessation of egg production to mark population elimination. Control cages averaged more than 10,000 eggs over the final month.
results.quote: We observe increases in frequency of the transgenic mosquitoes within the populations in all four cages initiated with the drive that lead to complete population suppression by 245–311 days after introduction.

results.finding: MM-CP Anopheles gambiae had 35 percentage points lower head or thorax parasite prevalence in replicate four (42 modified mosquitoes, 143 wild-type controls).
results.detail: The fifth replicate also showed lower parasite prevalence in the modified mosquitoes, with very low parasite levels in the positives.
results.quote:
none (0%) tested positive for parasites in their head and/or thorax, 
a proxy for salivary gland infection (Fig. 5d). By contrast, 82 (57%) of 
143 wt control mosquitoes were midgut positive and 50 (35%) had head 
and/or thorax parasite presence, showing variable sporozoite loads.

results.finding: SC Johnson Guardian reduced laboratory Anopheles gambiae landings by 98% overall, with 1,200 free-flying mosquitoes per arm.
results.detail: Two units were installed in the volunteer’s room. Mosquitoes could move between two connected rooms during the one-hour exposure.
results.quote:
Over 
the 12-month testing period, SC Johnson Guardian reduced mosquito -human landings by greater than 
95% for all four test systems.

results.finding: Guardian achieved 47.9% month-12 landing inhibition in Tanzania, with 2,231 Anopheles arabiensis caught in treated huts and 4,209 in control huts.
results.detail: The Benin results cover four months of a planned 12-month trial. The Mozambique Shield comparison was not used in decision-making.

results.finding: Mass ivermectin reduced adjusted malaria infection incidence by 26% versus albendazole among 2,606 children in 84 randomized clusters in Kwale, Kenya.
results.detail: The primary model used an independence correlation structure after the planned exchangeable model failed to converge.

results.finding: Children in Star Homes (247 at baseline) had 44% lower clinical malaria incidence than children in traditional homes (936 at baseline).
results.detail: Both arms recorded 98% bednet use during observed visits in the final year. Cross-sectional PCR surveys detected no significant between-arm difference in parasite prevalence.

results.finding: WHO issued a conditional recommendation in 2025 for indoor spatial emanators in areas with ongoing malaria transmission. Trial sample size is unreported.
results.detail: WHO advises sustaining target coverage with treated nets or indoor residual spraying when adding spatial emanators. The guideline development group identified continuous high coverage of the emanators as important for protection.
results.quote:
Spatial emanators can be deployed for the prevention and control of malaria in children and adults in areas with
ongoing malaria transmission.

results.finding: WHO’s 2019 conditional recommendation supports supplementary larviciding where aquatic habitats are few, fixed and findable. Trial sample size is unreported.
results.detail: WHO cites low certainty of evidence, impact limited to non-extensive habitats and feasibility concerns.
results.quote:
Insecticides can be regularly applied to water bodies (larviciding) for the prevention and control of malaria in children
and adults as a supplementary intervention to ITNs or IRS in areas with ongoing malaria transmission where aquatic
habitats are few, fixed and findable.

results.finding: WHO lists one Bti larvicide, VectoBac WG, as actively prequalified since 13 March 2018.
results.detail: WHO links to the product’s Statement of Conversion and Letter of Prequalification.

results.finding: AcTP13 mosquitoes (n = 53) had 52.1% lower salivary-gland sporozoite prevalence than wild-type controls (n = 48).
results.detail: The low-challenge assay had relatively low infectivity in controls. In the parallel medium-challenge assay, AcTP13 still significantly reduced sporozoite prevalence, with a smaller effect.
results.quote: Corresponding sporozoite numbers also were significantly lower, with prevalence showing a 52.1% reduction ( P  = 0.0418), mean sporozoite loads showing an 80.3 % reduction ( P  = 0.0139), and no salivary gland samples having >10,000 sporozoites.

results.finding: Chinese malaria surveillance classified 72 of 320 investigated foci as residual non-active.
results.detail: The response evaluation used matched surveillance records and included residual non-active foci linked to indigenous cases reported in 2013–2014.
results.quote:
The 320 foci were investigated and classified as 24 ac-
tive foci, 72 residual non-active foci, and 224 cleared-up
foci.

results.finding: Mosquito Shield reduced An. arabiensis landings by 38.09% on days 31–32 in Tanzania (38,375 mosquitoes captured across both arms over 32 days).
results.detail: Table 5 gives no Tanzania capture count for days 31–32. The final-interval confidence interval spans the 30% landing threshold. Benin’s blood-feeding result was pooled across 32 days.

results.finding: In 55 Namibian clusters, added reactive focal indoor spraying reduced adjusted incidence of confirmed locally acquired malaria by 52%.
results.detail: The pooled control included both routine reactive case detection and the experimental mass drug administration arm, with the same drug allocation factor in the spraying group. Statistical significance came from the adjusted analysis. The crude comparison had p=0.41.
results.quote: lower in clusters receiving RAVC than in those that did not (0·48 [0·16–0·80], p=0·002)

results.finding: Insecticidal hammocks in Vietnam (4,103 tested in late 2005) yielded a 0.62 ratio of changes in malaria infection odds versus control.
results.detail: Baseline prevalence differed between arms, so the analysis compared changes from baseline. The between-arm difference in those changes was no longer statistically significant at the final survey.
results.quote:
The difference between
intervention and control groups was at the highest during the last
semester of 2005 and the first of 2006 when the interaction terms
were 0.62 (95%CI [0.48; 0.79]) and 0.63 (95%CI [0.42; 0.96]),
respectively, indicating a 1.6-fold greater reduction in the
intervention than in the control group.

results.finding: On Aneityum, microscopy and PCR detected zero Plasmodium infections among 929 participants surveyed in June 2015.
results.detail: Larvivorous fish were introduced alongside insecticide-treated nets, mass drug administration, and surveillance. The study did not estimate their separate contribution.

definition = "An additional measure directed at malaria-transmitting mosquitoes helps stop transmission in a focus, a bounded area where local conditions allow the parasite to spread. Transmission had persisted there despite effective use of insecticide-treated nets or insecticide sprayed on indoor surfaces. Indoor spatial repellents have reduced new infections in children using treated nets. Interruption goes further: local mosquitoes cease passing the parasite to people, although infections acquired elsewhere can still be detected.". Reason: The definition leaves “focus” unexplained and gives readers no example of the difference between reducing infections and interrupting transmission.

goal.need = "In 30 communities in southwestern Mali, 93.2% of people surveyed used a net and 34% had malaria infection. Net users still received an estimated 11.2 malaria-vector bites per person per night, 7.1 of them outdoors. Nets protect people in bed, and indoor spraying reaches mosquitoes that rest on treated surfaces. Preventing infections in people exposed elsewhere depends on reaching the mosquitoes responsible for those bites. If local transmission stops, surveillance and measures to prevent its return are still needed.". Reason: The regional share of all malaria cases does not quantify the gap in protection experienced by people who use nets.

add statement by World Health Organization, 2014: "specifically designed to interrupt residual transmission and thereby address the practical limitations of existing interventions". Reason: WHO’s guidance note explicitly asks for tools that interrupt residual transmission.

edit completion: title = "An added vector intervention helps stop locally acquired malaria in a focus for more than three years."; criterion = "In a defined focus with transmission persisting despite effective use of treated nets or indoor residual spraying, comparative field evidence establishes that an additional mosquito-directed intervention contributed to interruption. Case investigation and surveillance document more than three years without a new locally acquired mosquito-borne infection, including one directly linked to an imported case. Investigators distinguish imported, relapsing, recrudescent and induced cases. Surveillance and measures against re-establishment continue."; set_by = "Atlas synthesis. WHO\u2019s 2017 framework supplies the cleared-focus endpoint. No outside body was found to combine it with attribution to an added vector intervention."; set_by_kind = "atlas"; threshold_quote = "There has been no locally acquired case for more than 3 years"; threshold_ref = 24; basis = "Table 3 of WHO\u2019s 2017 framework uses locally acquired cases. Table 4 of WHO\u2019s 2025 surveillance manual uses indigenous cases for its operational time criterion and allows only imported, relapsing, recrudescent or induced cases in the current calendar year. The Atlas retains the 2017 rule: a new local mosquito-borne infection directly linked to an imported case also restarts the interval. Comparative evidence establishes the intervention\u2019s contribution in the evaluated setting."; refs = [24, 23, 6]. Reason: The title implies sole causation, and the criterion needs to identify which WHO case definition starts the three-year clock.

edit m1: criterion = "A controlled laboratory comparison shows a reduction in mosquito abundance, the mosquitoes\u2019 ability to transmit the parasite, or mosquito contact with people, according to the intervention\u2019s intended effect. For a spatial emanator, a relevant measure is the reduction in mosquito landings on people relative to a control."; set_by = "WHO/TDR, Guidance framework for testing genetically modified mosquitoes, section 2.6.1, for suppression and modification. WHO\u2019s Guardian efficacy assessment documents the laboratory comparison for a spatial emanator."; threshold_quote = "the primary objective should be the potential for reducing transmission intensity"; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7, 14]. Reason: The laboratory criterion includes published results and cites guidance for genetically modified mosquitoes as its only basis for testing all three approaches.

add milestone after m1: "A spatial emanator demonstrates end-of-life efficacy in three semi-field studies.". Reason: WHO specifies a semi-field efficacy stage for spatial emanators between controlled room tests and evidence of protection in people.

edit m2: title = "An added vector intervention significantly reduces human malaria infection in a controlled field trial."; criterion = "A controlled field trial shows a statistically significant reduction in its prespecified human malaria infection endpoint relative to a control arm receiving the local standard of care. The trial specifies its target effect size and significance level in advance. Mosquito abundance, landings and infectious bites alone do not measure infection in people."; set_by = "WHO, Norms, standards and processes underpinning WHO vector control policy development, sections on trial endpoints and epidemiological outcomes."; set_by_kind = "government_programme"; threshold_quote = "a statistically significant epidemiological impact over the control arm"; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 10]. Reason: WHO provides a field-trial criterion applicable across interventions, while the two significance boundaries in the entry belong to one Kenya trial.
